name: workspace
//: Depends on every other project so the cross-cutting checks run whenever anything they check can change. Without these edges a crate-only change would skip the graph check that keeps affected selection honest. llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] JSON has no comment to scope this to the `test` target below, which is what it is about. Those clone-based checks are cross-cutting by construction: what each drives — the git hooks, the gate's provisioning, the Nx graph itself, the plugin-isolation rule — is owned by no product project, so there is no narrower project to put them behind, and the edges above are exactly what makes them run when anything they check changes.

bootstrap.//: Uncached: it installs toolchain components and activates the git hooks path, both outside the tree.

options.command: bun run biome format --write nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

format.//: Uncached: it rewrites the tree in place.

options.command: bun run biome format nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

commands: bun run biome lint --error-on-warnings nx.json biome.json package.json .claude workspace crates sdks

test.//: Uncached: three checks clone a repository and read git history, which no input glob in this tree describes — a cached pass would assert about a graph that has since changed. Serial because those checks each clone into a scratch tree and run cargo or Nx there; racing them would contend for the same registry lock for no gain. The isolation concurrency check creates its own intentional fan-out inside that serial target. check-hook-safety runs first and takes milliseconds: it proves the scratch-clone helper the three later cloning checks depend on still survives the environment a git hook gives it, and if that has broken, their results below are about the wrong repository. check-pre-push-provisioning drives the real hook in an unprovisioned clone, which is what keeps a fresh worktree's missing toolchain from reading as a rejected push.

test-live.//: Uncached for the same reason as every other test-live target: the live lane's result depends on credentials and third-party services that are not inputs in this tree.

commands: cargo deny check bans licenses sources

deny.//: Uncached: `cargo deny check advisories` fetches the RustSec advisory database, so a clean tree can start failing without a single file changing — which is the point of running it.
